node.statement: For X=U bold-dot V, the operator L_X differs from the invertible operator L_U composed with L_V by at most epsilon_r||U||||V||<=4*epsilon_r in operator norm. Node 1.2 gives ||(L_U composed with L_V)^{-1}||<=9, so 36*epsilon_r<=9/16<1 and the elementary Neumann perturbation lemma makes L_X invertible. Hence X has a right inverse.
